extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Patent Office officials, legislators, patent attorneys, and inventors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and recommended statutory/administrative changes for Patent Office practice (use and preservation of models, reissue practice, fees, interferences, organization, and copy-pricing) drawn from the 1877 Commissioner report. Aimed at improving examination uniformity, preventing fraud, and reducing burdens on inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Models required only in specific circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Models form no part of the patent; the specification and drawing must disclose fully the invention; examinations can be made without models and with greater certainty from drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require models only where: (a) the capability of the machine to operate is in question; (b) the Examiner doubts the sufficiency of the drawing; or (c) models are necessary for ready illustration on appeals or in interference cases. Omit general requirement for models to relieve inventors of expense and to encourage fuller, clearer drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation limited to valuable working models
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve such models as shall be capable of operation and be deemed valuable for illustrating practical working machines used anywhere in the country; receive specimens of manufacture and working models for exhibition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form a collection confined to inventions actually in use (working models) rather than retaining the great mass of accumulated models; this will illustrate the state of the arts while requiring much less space and avoiding useless material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue limited to matter in specification and drawing (no reliance on models)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrict the applicant for reissue to matters contained in the specification and drawing, without any reference to the model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the model is not part of the patent and not brought to public notice, allowing reissues based on model-only matter may surprise the public and give opportunity for fraud (including alteration of models). Modify the law to prohibit introducing matter shown only in models into reissues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disallow reissue amendments based on proof outside Office record
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue practice that permits introduction of new matter upon reissue based on proof outside the Office record (voluntary affidavits) creates opportunity for fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modify/repeal the provision (latter part of section 4916 Revised Statutes as understood) permitting reissue amendments based on proof outside the Office; avoid accepting voluntary affidavits as a basis for introducing new matter on reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative correction mechanism for inventor attribution errors
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be provision to correct honest mistakes (e.g., parties named as joint inventors when some were only assignees) where reissue does not apply and the Department has held the correction cannot be made as a clerical error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorize the Commissioner to receive such patents with proper affidavits of the parties interested, make the correction, and issue a proper certificate of correction—avoiding the need for reissue in such cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic maintenance fees to remove frivolous patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents of little or no value and trivial improvements are frequently granted; some patents retard progress and bring the system into disrepute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require payment of fees at certain periods in the life of a patent as a condition to continuation; this natural-selection-like process would tend to remove useless/frivolous patents without seriously burdening meritorious ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend final fee timing to align issue date and patent term start (section 4885)
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing law requires payment of the final fee within six months after notice of allowance, but Office issue-closing practices can make it impossible to give the patent the intended issue date if the fee is paid on the last legal day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change the law so papers can be prepared and ready for delivery on the day the patent term begins; adjust the timing rules so the Office can close weekly issues and sign patents without resorting to administrative fictions or signing patents in blank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove restriction tying US patent term to foreign patent term (section 4887)
rubrics_metrics.description: Last clause of section 4887 requires every U.S. patent for an invention previously patented abroad to be so limited as to expire at the same time with the foreign patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no good reason for this restriction; it imposes an undue limitation on citizens. Alternatively, to prevent foreign patentees from exploiting the U.S. system, require timely U.S. applications (e.g., within two years of the foreign patent) rather than automatic term alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal treatment for applications forfeited for non-payment and abandoned applications (section 4897)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications forfeited for non-payment of the final fee are treated differently from applications abandoned by failure to act within two years after Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amend the law so that applications forfeited for non-payment of the final fee are placed upon the same basis as abandoned applications; eliminate the discrimination against cases passed for issue but neglected as to final fee payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit post-decision interferences with successful party's application (section 4904)
rubrics_metrics.description: After final decision between parties to an interference, the successful party's application should not be put in interference with any application filed after the closing of testimony taken on behalf of the successful party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permit only an interference of subsequent parties with the patent of the prevailing party (not with his pending application) to avoid parties defeated in an interference from filing new applications or using third parties to prolong proceedings and delay patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make copy-pricing equitable (section 493)
rubrics_metrics.description: Current prices: manuscript copies 10c per 100 words; printed copies 25c per single copy and 10c each for 20+; certified printed copies cost the same as manuscript copies—resulting in what the report calls 'exorbitant' prices for certified printed copies and excessive prices for large sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amend section 493 so pricing is more equitable—reduce excessive charges for certified printed copies and for large orders (several hundreds or thousands of copies) to reflect actual cost and fairness to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use drawings/photolithograph copies for examinations and infringement inquiries when models absent
rubrics_metrics.description: With models destroyed or omitted, preliminary and infringement examinations can be made by means of copies of the drawings (photolithographs) which may substitute for physical models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproduce and maintain sets of photolithograph copies to supply the place of models; rely on drawings for clearer, fuller examination and avoid dependence on physical models for routine examination and infringement review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reorganize Office and create permanent appellate tribunal (patent court)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present organization (many Principal Examiners, little review of favorable actions, frequent changes in Board membership, and Commissioner saddled with judicial duties) leads to lack of uniformity and excessive patent grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group classes to place grant responsibility in fewer hands; relieve the Commissioner of judicial/appeal duties; establish a permanent tribunal (a patent court of three members appointed like U.S. judges) to hear appeals directly from Examiners, provide stable judicial leadership, and enable the Commissioner to focus on executive supervision and inspection of patents.
